The Church Board of Education is composed of the First Presidency and other general authorities and officers, including the presidents of the Relief Society and Young Women organizations. This board oversees all of the church schools, including universities, seminaries, institutes, and other schools. (William E. Berrett, “Church Educational System [CES],” inEncyclopedia of Mormonism,ed. Daniel H. Ludlow, 5 vols. [New York: Macmillan, 1992], 1:275.)

W. Grant Bangerter served his first mission to Brazil from 1939 to 1941 and was president of the Brazilian Mission from 1958 to 1963. He joined the First Quorum of the Seventy in 1975 and served twice in its presidency, from 1978 to 1980 and from 1985 to 1989. (Arave, “Elder William Grant Bangerter Dies at 91.”)

The consolidated meeting schedule was implemented in 1980; it grouped sacrament, Sunday School, Melchizedek and Aaronic Priesthood, Relief Society, Young Women, and Primary meetings into a three-hour time block on Sunday. (Hal Knight, “Meeting Schedule Approved,”Church News,Feb. 2, 1980.)
